title: Guide pratique menant à la caractérisation de la douleur chez l'animal de compagnie
author: Eric Troncy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uw4exgw
materials:
- Réalisez l’examen clinique du patient
1
- Dans l'image ci-dessus, indiquez par un cercle l’endroit où les tests d’hyperalgésie1/allodynie2 primaire mécanique seront effectués. Si le site principal de la douleur est profond, s’il vous plaît sélectionnez un emplacement aussi proche que possible, ou encore indiquez N/D (non disponible) dans un cercle.
Hyperalgésie/allodynie primaire mécanique
2
- Indiquez avec une flèche (nom entre parenthèses, si nécessaire) la source primaire de la douleur suspectée du patient
3
1Réfère à une sensation de douleur exagérée en réponse à un stimulus normalement douloureux
2Sensation de douleur en réponse à un stimulus normalement inoffensif.

steps.title: Initial visual and tactile assessment
steps.instruction: Observe skin temperature (record as normal or elevated/calor), gently touch the area, and record yes/no for pain on touch (dolor), redness (rubor), and swelling (tumor).

steps.title: Sharp tactile threshold (von Frey)
steps.instruction: Apply the von Frey filament to the test site, repeat the stimulus three times with a 10‑second interval between applications, record each threshold value, then wait 1 minute before the next procedure.

steps.title: Mechanical pressure threshold (Wagner sensor)
steps.instruction: Using the Wagner mechanical pressure sensor, apply pressure to the test site, repeat three times with a 10‑second interval between applications, record each threshold, and wait 1 minute after completing the three measurements.

steps.title: Dynamic brushing response (optional)
steps.instruction: Brush the test area with a soft brush and note the latency of any withdrawal response; record the time if a response occurs. Mark as non‑applicable if not performed.

steps.title: Secondary hyperalgesia with cuff inflation
steps.instruction: Gently lift the dog’s paw and massage from the foot toward the elbow (or knee). Place a cuff around the mid‑radius or mid‑tibia and inflate it to 200 mmHg. Encourage the dog to walk in the room for 2 minutes. Then repeat the Wagner pressure test at the primary pain site four times: measurements 1 and 2 while the cuff remains inflated, then deflate the cuff and record measurements 3 and 4. Keep a 10‑second interval between each measurement.

steps.title: Diffuse nociceptive inhibitor control
steps.instruction: Select four random sites on the lateral margin of the longissimus muscle (e.g., lateral to the 11th vertebra and immediately caudal to the 13th vertebra). For each of three measurement rounds, apply the Wagner pressure sensor at each of the four sites, recording the pressure threshold. Keep a 10‑second interval between individual site measurements and wait 1 minute between the three rounds.
